decisive_items: brain MRI showed chronic periventricular white matter changes
A diagnostic algorithm for dizziness suggested a low probability of central or peripheral vestibular origin
Review of the CTA suggested that carotid stenosis had been overestimated due to marked vessel tortuosity
response.rationale: Chronic periventricular white matter changes are the most concrete finding supporting small vessel disease, while the vestibular algorithm and vascular work-up (CTA overestimation, normal TCD hemodynamics, no recent MRI lesions) exclude other candidates; remaining options are either contradicted or lack adequate support.

rejected.why: Only dizziness worsened by movement/position is present; no cervical spine findings or supporting evidence.
Atherosclerosis was overestimated on CTA; TCD showed normal hemodynamics.
Carotid stenosis was explicitly overestimated and contradicted by normal hemodynamics.
Algorithm indicated low probability of central or peripheral vestibular origin.
No orthostatic vital signs or typical orthostatic pattern; Romberg and truncal ataxia not explained.
No recent vascular lesions on MRI; normal TCD hemodynamics argue against active cerebrovascular disease.
Low vestibular probability and normal vascular imaging/hemodynamics exclude vertebrobasilar insufficiency.
